messages:
Anna: Heads-up — customer reported a billing spike during a streamed completion + toolcall. Console showed provisional tokens and then a refund, but ledger has a couple of provisional entries that never consolidated. Suspect routing switch mid-stream + truncation handshake.
Matt: Can you paste the session id / headers we got?
Anna: sess-abc123. Logs (sanitized):
```
STREAM_START session=sess-abc123 model=rwx-3k route=canary-1
TOKEN_EMIT count=312 prefix_hash=0x7f3
TOOLCALL_START tool=search tokens_consumed=311
TOOLCALL_TRUNCATE at_token=311 reason=client_timeout
RETRY route=main resume_session=sess-abc123 resume_offset=300
STREAM_RESUME tokens_emitted=339
LEDGER_WRITE type=provisional id=prov-aaa session=sess-abc123 tokens=311
LEDGER_WRITE type=provisional id=prov-bbb session=sess-abc123 tokens=339
LEDGER_WRITE type=confirm id=conf-ccc session=sess-abc123 tokens=650
```
Anna: Note the two provisional writes, different ids, then one confirm that sums to 650 (311+339), but console UI showed a provisional spike of ~650 then a 311 refund. Means we recorded provisional twice and later the UX deduped wrong.
Kevin: Interesting. Looks like when route changed we treated the resumed stream as a separate provisional write (new provisional id). We rely on client-provided session id but resume creates a new provisional id. If the console dedupe key is prefix_hash it will sometimes collapse incorrectly (or incorrectly attribute the smaller one as the final).
Matt: Do we have an invariant for provisional -> confirm flow? I thought confirm should reference the canonical provisional id.
Kevin: Right today confirm only references session and total tokens, not the set of provisional ids. That makes it hard to reconcile when multiple provis were emitted for same session across routes.
Sylvia: From console/ops UX POV we show provisional by provisional-id; when two show up we surface both. The "refund" was actually us removing the smaller provisional and showing the larger one as final (so UI showed negative adjustment). That's very confusing for customers.
Anna: Customer impact: visible temporary overage alerts and a billing email. They weren't actually overcharged but the churn alarm hit the team.
Matt: Short term: can we add an aggregation in the ledger worker that merges provisional records for same session within a 5s grace window and emit a single combined provisional id (or at least tag them)? Would avoid UI flip.
Kevin: That would help UI but still leaves the accounting invariant fuzzy. Better long term: make confirms reference "provisional_set_id" (or allow confirm to include list of provisional ids). Then ledger can atomically mark related provisionals confirmed once.
Kevin: Proposed API change: confirm request body adds optional field "provisional_ids": ["prov-aaa","prov-bbb"] and ledger will dedupe by that. Backwards compatible — if absent, fallback to session-level reconcile.
Matt: Sounds good. Any perf/cost concerns?
Kevin: Minimal — metadata only. The tricky part is callers (runtime + router) need to track the provisional ids produced on each route resume. Router already receives provisionals from the worker; we need to plumb them to the final confirm path.
Sylvia: UX ask: surface "provisional (pending confirmation)" and keep both entries visible until confirm, but annotate merges/confirmations. Also add a tooltip: "If your session was routed mid-stream we may temporarily show multiple provisional entries."
Anna: Telemetry: we should emit a metric count.provisional_fragments_per_confirm and a tag route_change=true|false. Then alert on >1% of streams having fragments.
Matt: ops-bot — can you create an alert ticket for that metric?
ops-bot: Created ticket #INF-4821 for metric and alert config (link: https://tickets.internal/INF-4821) :white_check_mark:
Infra CI Bot: Build for ledger branch with provisional_set support passed: https://ci.internal/builds/ledger/7823 :package:
Kevin: I'll open an RFC and a small PR to accept provisional_ids on confirm. Will also update runtime to collect prov ids on resume and forward them.
Sylvia: I'll file a console PR to change UI to show "pending fragments" and not cancel until confirm.
Anna: Action items: Kevin -> RFC + PR; Sylvia -> console UI patch; Matt -> prioritize dashboard metric/alerting; Anna -> follow up with customer and explain temporary UI churn.
Matt: Timeline? Kevin: can do RFC + tiny API change in next 3 days, then deploy to canary. Sylvia: UI tweak in a week. Matt: OK, set canary flag for new confirm param and test with internal load.
Anna: Thanks all. If anyone notices other sessions with similar pattern, drop them here (session ids). :thumbsup:
